forces.title: Production Linked Incentive scheme boosts food processing capacity and exports
forces.description: The PLISFPI, with an outlay of US$ 1.23 billion, has successfully attracted US$ 1.04 billion in investments. This scheme has facilitated the creation of approximately 35 lakh MT of processing capacity and generated around 3.3 lakh jobs. It significantly boosts processed food exports with a 13.23% CAGR (2019-2025) and promotes Indian brands internationally, directly benefiting processed meat, poultry, and seafood.

forces.title: US tariffs pose significant headwind for India's shrimp exports
forces.description: India's shrimp exports are expected to moderate by 10-12% in FY26, primarily due to adverse US tariff headwinds. The US, which historically accounted for ~40% of total exports, showed only muted 5% growth in 5M FY26, with a sharp 35% decline in August 2025 from July, indicating substantial pressure from trade policies.

forces.title: Supportive investment in animal husbandry infrastructure via AHIDF scheme
forces.description: The Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF) scheme provides a substantial US$ 3.5 billion outlay, offering a 3% interest subvention for private investments. As of December 2025, 465 projects worth US$ 2.55 billion have been approved, directly promoting critical infrastructure development for livestock, which underpins the meat and poultry sub-segments.

forces.title: Expanded cold chain and reefer vehicle infrastructure strengthens logistics
forces.description: Integrated cold chain projects are experiencing rapid expansion, with 404 projects underway. This initiative will add 10.06 lakh MT of cold storage capacity and introduce 1918 reefer vehicles by FY26. This infrastructure is critically important for preserving the quality, extending the shelf life, and broadening the distribution reach of perishable meat, poultry, and seafood products.

forces.title: Favorable FDI policy attracts investment in food processing sector
forces.description: India's policy permitting 100% Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) under the automatic route in the food processing sector serves as a significant tailwind. This liberal policy attracts substantial foreign capital, driving expansion, technological advancements, and increased production capacity across the entire food processing industry, including the meat, poultry, and seafood segments.

forces.title: Robust raw material base supports meat, poultry, and seafood production
forces.description: India possesses the world's largest livestock base and ranks as the fifth-largest meat producer. Furthermore, it is the third-largest fish producer, contributing 8% to global output, and ranks second in aquaculture. This extensive and diverse raw material supply offers a significant competitive advantage and a stable foundation for the meat, poultry, and seafood processing industries.

forces.title: Population growth and changing habits drive demand for animal proteins
forces.description: India, maintaining a young demographic until 2030, is experiencing rapid population growth, rising disposable incomes, and significant urbanization. These factors, combined with evolving food preferences, are substantially increasing the demand for processed food, including meat, poultry, and seafood, creating a robust domestic market for the sector.

forces.title: Expected moderation in operating margins for shrimp export sector
forces.description: Operating margins for the shrimp export sector are projected to moderate by 150 basis points, primarily anticipated in FY27. This moderation is driven by competitive pressures within the global market. Despite the growth in value-added shrimp products, which typically support margins, the overall environment suggests a challenging period for profitability.

forces.title: Increased food tech and online grocery penetration boosts demand
forces.description: The stable growth in food tech, with 17% GMV increase and high user engagement, coupled with the online grocery market projected to grow at a 32.7% CAGR to US$ 76.76 billion by 2032, creates a strong tailwind. This digital adoption and convenience drive increased demand for packaged and ready-to-eat meat, poultry, and seafood products.

forces.title: APEDA's BHARATI initiative strengthens agri-food export readiness and innovation
forces.description: The BHARATI initiative launched by APEDA is designed to empower 100 agri-food and agri-tech startups, fostering innovation and improving export readiness. This program targets achieving US$ 50 billion in agri-food exports by 2030, directly enhancing the capabilities and global competitiveness of processed meat, poultry, and seafood products for international markets.

forces.title: Fiscal benefits and priority lending support food processing investments
forces.description: Food processing units benefit from fiscal incentives such as full profit exemptions for five years and 100% capital expenditure deductions for cold chains and warehouses. Additionally, loans to these units qualify as Agriculture under Priority Sector Lending (PSL), providing access to affordable credit and significantly easing financial burdens for operators in the meat, poultry, and seafood sectors.

forces.title: Strategic coastal access enhances seafood export potential globally
forces.description: India's extensive 7,500+ km coastline and strategic coastal access are crucial for facilitating smooth trade. This geographic advantage enables efficient connectivity with major international markets in Europe, the Middle East, Africa (west coast), and Asia-Pacific (east coast), significantly boosting the export potential for marine products and seafood processors in India.

forces.title: Diversification to non-U.S. markets drives incremental shrimp export growth
forces.description: Non-U.S. destinations for shrimp exports surged by 30% year-on-year in 5M FY26, contributing nearly 86% of the incremental export value. Strong demand from markets like China, Vietnam (serving as a re-export hub), Belgium, and the EU, alongside enhanced compliance, indicates a strategic and successful shift away from historically U.S.-centric exports, creating new growth avenues.

forces.title: Redesigning shrimp supply chain for global competitiveness and resilience
forces.description: To achieve its full potential, India must proactively accelerate bilateral trade agreements and evolve beyond reactive export strategies for shrimp. Designing a resilient, demand-driven, and geopolitically balanced supply chain is identified as a critical upside driver. This strategic re-design will enhance long-term growth, stability, and global market positioning for the seafood industry.

forces.title: Food irradiation units improve product safety and shelf life
forces.description: An additional outlay of US$ 219 million under the PMKSY is allocated for establishing 50 Multi-Product Food Irradiation Units within the Integrated Cold Chain and Value Addition Infrastructure. These units are crucial for enhancing food safety standards, significantly extending the shelf life, and supporting value addition for highly perishable products like meat, poultry, and seafood.

forces.title: RBI relief measures ease liquidity pressures for exporters
forces.description: Recent relief measures implemented by the RBI, including temporary moratoriums and extended export credit tenures, are expected to significantly ease liquidity pressures for exporters in the near term. This financial support is crucial for the shrimp export sector, which faces external challenges, helping to stabilize cash flows and operational capabilities during uncertain periods.

forces.title: Government budget increases for food processing sector development
forces.description: The Union Budget FY27 allocates US$ 459.88 million (Rs. 4064 Crore) to the Ministry for Food Processing Sector development, marking a 13.79% increase from FY26. This growing governmental financial support ensures continued investment in schemes like PMKSY, PLI, and PMFME, fostering overall growth and modernization within the food processing industry, including meat, poultry, and seafood segments.

viewpoints.title: India's shrimp export outlook remains cautious due to US tariffs
viewpoints.description: CareEdge Ratings anticipates a moderation of 10-12% in India's shrimp exports for FY26. This cautious outlook is primarily driven by significant US tariff headwinds, which have already shown impact with a 35% month-on-month decline in August 2025. While diversification to non-U.S. markets provides some cushioning, the U.S. market, a major destination, is experiencing muted growth, signaling a challenging period for exporters.

viewpoints.title: Shrimp export operating margins expected to moderate in FY27 amidst competitive pressures
viewpoints.description: CareEdge Ratings projects a moderation of 150 basis points in operating margins for shrimp exports, particularly expected in FY27. This pressure on profitability is attributed to heightened competitive dynamics in the market. Although the growing share of value-added shrimp products provides some support, the overall trend suggests a challenging environment for maintaining margin levels for exporters.

viewpoints.title: Strategic re-evaluation crucial for India's shrimp export potential
viewpoints.description: CareEdge Ratings highlights the imperative for India to accelerate bilateral trade agreements and adopt a proactive, rather than reactive, export strategy for shrimp. To unlock its full potential, the nation must design a resilient, demand-driven, and geopolitically balanced supply chain. This strategic shift is vital for long-term growth and global competitiveness in the seafood sector.

demand_drivers.description: Sustained international demand for animal products, including processed and raw forms, drives export volumes and value from India.
India's ability to export a diverse range of animal products contributes to the overall export value.

market_sizing.methodology: Total export value of Animal products from India during the April-August 2025 period (FY26).

demand_drivers.description: Strong demand from non-U.S. destinations like China (16% growth), Vietnam (doubled), and Belgium (doubled) drives incremental export value, reflecting successful market diversification.
The growing share of value-added shrimp products, surging 27% globally and 78% in non-U.S. markets, supports export value and margins.

pnl_drivers.description: Increased production and export of value-added shrimp products are expected to support and potentially enhance operating margins.

new_opportunities.description: Improved compliance by Indian players in markets like the EU and the potential for new bilateral trade agreements can open up further export opportunities.

market_sizing.methodology: Total export value and volume of shrimp from India during the first five months of FY26 (April-August 2025). The methodology includes analyzing growth drivers by destination market.

demand_drivers.description: Increasing population, urbanization, and higher disposable incomes are driving overall food consumption and demand for protein-rich products like eggs.
Evolving dietary preferences and increasing awareness of protein benefits contribute to higher egg consumption.

market_sizing.methodology: Historical growth rate of egg production in India over the past decade. Production volume for 2024-25 is also provided.

demand_drivers.description: Focus on developing cold storage, abattoirs, and food parks directly supports the growth and expansion of the processed food industry, including meat, poultry, and seafood.
Growing consumer preference for processed and ready-to-eat food items contributes to the overall market expansion.

new_opportunities.description: Significant opportunities exist for investment in and development of cold chain infrastructure and modern abattoirs to enhance processing, storage, and distribution capabilities for meat, poultry, and seafood.
